name: Jalāl al-Dīn Abū al-Faḍl ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr al-Suyūṭī
summary: The most prolific author of Mamluk Cairo, who gathered the whole of naḥw in Hamʿ al-hawāmiʿ, gave it its 'principles' in al-Iqtirāḥ, and wrote the lives of the grammarians in Bughyat al-wuʿāt.
bio: Al-Suyūṭī was born in Cairo in 849/1445, his family from Asyūṭ, and studied with some of the last great teachers of the Mamluk age; in grammar with al-Shumunnī and with al-Kāfiyajī, whom he served for fourteen years. At forty he withdrew from teaching to his house on the island of Rawḍa and wrote, by his own count, several hundred books, on every science of the madrasa.

In naḥw his Jamʿ al-jawāmiʿ, with his own commentary Hamʿ al-hawāmiʿ, gathers the views of the grammarians on every question in a single order, the last great summa of the subject. His al-Bahja al-marḍiyya is a short commentary on the Alfiyya, much read in the Ottoman lands as 'Suyūṭī'; al-Ashbāh wa-l-naẓāʾir fī al-naḥw collects its general rules; al-Iqtirāḥ fī uṣūl al-naḥw sets out its principles, after Ibn Jinnī and Ibn al-Anbārī; and al-Muzhir gathers what was known of the Arabic language itself.

His Bughyat al-wuʿāt fī ṭabaqāt al-lughawiyyīn wa-l-nuḥāt, the lives of the grammarians and lexicographers in alphabetical order, more than two thousand of them, is the last of the classical ṭabaqāt and the one most consulted. He died in 911/1505.
